figures.finding: The legal working age is eighteen; from sixteen, with the parents' or legal representative's authorisation or the Ministry of Labour's approval, a minor may do light work that harms neither health, safety, morals, development nor schooling, provided he has had training in that line of work, and never dangerous work. Artists (those who agree to give artistic services to an organiser of public shows for pay) are a special relation the Law leaves to a special provision, which wasn't found; under sixteen the Law gives no route for a performer. The same rule holds for a young writer or director employed.

value.permit: from 16: parents'/legal representative's authorisation or Ministry of Labour approval (light work only)

figures.finding: Equatorial Guinea is a party to the OHADA Treaty (in force there from 1999-08-13), so its company law is OHADA's: a minor who is not emancipated may not be a trader or do commercial acts (Uniform Act on general commercial law, art. 7), and minors may be partners only in a company where they are not liable for its debts beyond their contribution (Uniform Act on commercial companies, art. 8), so a young producer's vehicle can be an SARL or SA in which the minor holds shares, never a general partnership; the Acts set no age of their own for a manager, and a person under a legal incapacity may not be a partner (art. 7), so the national age of majority governs.

Une personne physique ou morale ne peut être associée dans une société commerciale lorsqu'elle fait l'objet d'une interdiction, incapacité ou incompatibilité prévue par une disposition légale ou réglementaire.
